body.text: In short:
A teenager is in a serious condition in hospital after several cars were engulfed in fire in Melbourne's outer north-west.
Two of the cars were parked in the driveway of a house and a third was on a nearby street corner.
In Airport West, also in the city's north-west, firefighters battled for two hours to control a blaze at a car workshop.
A teenager has been rushed to hospital with significant burns after an incident in the suburb of Taylors Hill, in Melbourne's north-west.
Paramedics and firefighters were called to Woolwich Way just after 5am to find a person and three cars on fire.
An Ambulance Victoria spokesperson said a teenage boy was found with upper and lower body injuries.
He was taken to the Royal Children's Hospital in a serious condition.
Police believe two cars parked in the driveway of a home were firebombed and that the teenager had tried to flee in the third vehicle, which had been stolen from Hoppers Crossing yesterday.
They say the car crashed into bushes and that two other people fled from the scene.
One person, who asked not to be named, woke up to their two cars on fire.
"I'm just in shock, I just can't believe what's happened," they told 774 ABC Melbourne.
"I'm angry, I'm upset."
Police believed it was a targeted attack, the person said.
They said they had seen the white car outside their house several times before and had confronted the driver but they did not know what they wanted.
A neighbour, who only wanted to known as Joe, said he used his garden tap to try to help the injured teenager.
"He looked like he was severely burnt. I tried to keep him wet as much as possible," he said.
"I didn't have a hose, so I used my hands. I turned the tap full blast and I tried to splash as much water as I possibly could on him."
Ivan Dragovic lives nearby and said he heard explosions.
"Someone came out of the car and started yelling: 'Help, help, help'," he said.
"When the ambulance arrived, they took him there across the road on the grass and tried to help him."
The Arson and Explosives Squad remained on the scene this morning.
"Once again, we see the devastating consequences of arson and the dangers facing young people who become involved in organised crime," Detective Inspector Chris Murray said.
"These groups often use teenagers because they believe they are less likely to attract attention or face the same consequences as adult offenders."
Detective Inspector Murray appealed to young people to consider the consequences.
"The risks are real, arson isn't worth your life. Don't risk being seriously injured, killed, or imprisoned carrying out attacks for organised crime figures who see you as disposable".
Premier Ben Carroll described the incident as a senseless act that has had life-changing consequences for the injured teenager.
"This will irreversibly change his life forever," he said.
He said there must be "zero tolerance" for firebombings by youth offenders in Melbourne.
"Live a life of purpose, get a job, go on and have a great life or go down that path of criminality and have a terrible life," Mr Carroll said.
Fire destroys workshop, prestige cars in Airport West
Police were also investigating a fire that destroyed a prestige car workshop and numerous vehicles at Airport West in Melbourne's north-west.
Several calls to Triple Zero (000) reported explosions inside Prestige Autoworks just after 1am.
Firefighters arrived within seven minutes to find the brick workshop fully alight, with flames spreading through the roof.
Fire Rescue Victoria Commander Mark Sinkinson said there were fears the building would collapse.
"We had to put a fair bit of water in there," he said.
"There was quite a fuel load with the amount of cars that you would find within a panel beating shop."
Commander Sinkinson said it was an intense firefight.
"The back walls have come in, the roof has collapsed, it's been a very hot and intense fire," he said.
More than 50 firefighters battled the blaze and three aerial appliances were brought in.
The extent of damage had stopped firefighters from doing an assessment to determine how many cars had been destroyed, he said.
"It's a total loss. The factory will need to be demolished and rebuilt."
It took more than two hours to bring the fire under control.
Paramedics were called to the scene, but there have been no reports of injuries.
A Victoria Police spokesperson said no one was believed to have been inside the auto workshop when the fire began.
They said the cause was still being investigated but it was being treated as suspicious.
"Due to structural damage, investigations at the scene will continue when it is safe to do so," the police spokesperson said.
Anyone who witnessed these incidents were urged to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.
